quotes.text_ko: 철학을 진지하게 원한다면 처음부터 사람들이 비웃고 조롱할 준비를 하라. 교만한 표정을 짓지 말고, 신이 맡긴 자리처럼 자신이 가장 옳다고 여기는 것에 굳게 머물러라.
quotes.text_source_en: If you have an earnest desire toward philosophy, prepare yourself from the very first to have the multitude laugh and sneer, and say, “He is returned to us a philosopher all at once”; and, “Whence this supercilious look?” Now, for your part, do not have a supercilious look indeed, but keep steadily to those things which appear best to you, as one appointed by God to this particular station.

quotes.text_ko: 누군가를 기쁘게 하려고 외적인 것에 마음을 돌리는 순간, 자신의 삶의 계획을 망쳤음을 알아라.
quotes.text_source_en: If you ever happen to turn your attention to externals, for the pleasure of anyone, be assured that you have ruined your scheme of life.

quotes.text_ko: ‘평판을 잃고 어디서도 아무것도 아닌 사람이 될 것이다’라는 생각으로 괴로워하지 마라. 불명예가 악이라면 남이 너를 악에 빠뜨릴 수는 없다.
quotes.text_source_en: Let not such considerations as these distress you: “I shall live in discredit and be nobody anywhere.” For if discredit be an evil, you can no more be involved in evil through another than in baseness.

quotes.text_source_en: Is anyone preferred before you at an entertainment, or in courtesies, or in confidential intercourse?

quotes.work: The Enchiridion

quotes.text_ko: 자연의 뜻은 우리 모두가 동의하는 일들을 통해 배울 수 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: The will of nature may be learned from things upon which we are all agreed.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 표적이 빗나가도록 세워진 것이 아니듯, 악의 본성도 세상에 목적처럼 세워진 것은 아니다.
quotes.text_source_en: As a mark is not set up for the sake of missing the aim, so neither does the nature of evil exist in the world.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion

quotes.text_ko: 누군가 네 몸을 지나가는 사람에게 넘겨주었다면 분명 화를 낼 것이다.
quotes.text_source_en: If a person had delivered up your body to some passer-by, you would certainly be angry.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 의무는 언제나 관계에 따라 정해진다.
quotes.text_source_en: Duties are universally measured by relations.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 신에 대한 경건의 핵심은 그들이 존재하며 우주를 정의롭고 선하게 다스린다는 올바른 생각을 갖는 데 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: Be assured that the essence of piety toward the gods lies in this—to form right opinions concerning them, as existing and as governing the universe justly and well.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 점술가를 찾을 때에는 결과가 무엇인지 몰라 배우러 간다는 사실을 기억하라. 그러나 철학적이라면 그 결과가 선인지 악인지는 이미 알고 있어야 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: When you have recourse to divination, remember that you know not what the event will be, and you come to learn it of the diviner; but of what nature it is you knew before coming; at least, if you are of philosophic mind.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 혼자 있을 때나 사람들과 함께 있을 때나 지킬 수 있는 성품과 태도를 먼저 자신에게 정해 두어라.
quotes.text_source_en: Begin by prescribing to yourself some character and demeanor, such as you may preserve both alone and in company.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 약속된 쾌락의 겉모습에 눈이 부시면 그것에 휩쓸리지 않도록 경계하라. 일을 잠시 미루고 스스로에게 생각할 시간을 주어라.
quotes.text_source_en: If you are dazzled by the semblance of any promised pleasure, guard yourself against being bewildered by it; but let the affair wait your leisure, and procure yourself some delay.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 분명한 판단으로 옳다고 여겨 행동했다면 세상이 오해하더라도 그 행동이 보이는 것을 두려워하지 마라. 옳지 않다면 행동 자체를 피하고, 옳다면 잘못 비난하는 사람을 왜 두려워하는가.
quotes.text_source_en: When you do anything from a clear judgment that it ought to be done, never shrink from being seen to do it, even though the world should misunderstand it; for if you are not acting rightly, shun the action itself; if you are, why fear those who wrongly censure you?
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion

quotes.text_ko: ‘낮이거나 밤이다’라는 말은 양자택일 논증에서는 강하지만 둘을 함께 묶는 논증에서는 쓸모없다. 잔치에서 가장 큰 몫을 고르는 것도 몸의 욕구에는 맞지만 함께하는 정신에는 맞지 않는다.
quotes.text_source_en: As the proposition, “either it is day or it is night,” has much force in a disjunctive argument, but none at all in a conjunctive one, so, at a feast, to choose the largest share is very suitable to the bodily appetite, but utterly inconsistent with the social spirit of the entertainment.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 힘에 넘치는 역할을 맡으면 그 역할도 제대로 하지 못하고, 감당할 수 있었던 역할마저 버리게 된다.
quotes.text_source_en: If you have assumed any character beyond your strength, you have both demeaned yourself ill in that and quitted one which you might have supported.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 걸을 때 못을 밟거나 발목을 접질리지 않게 조심하듯, 마음을 다스리는 능력이 상하지 않도록 조심하라.
quotes.text_source_en: As in walking you take care not to tread upon a nail, or turn your foot, so likewise take care not to hurt the ruling faculty of your mind.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 신발의 크기가 발에 맞아야 하듯, 각자의 소유는 몸의 필요를 기준으로 해야 한다.
quotes.text_source_en: The body is to everyone the proper measure of its possessions, as the foot is of the shoe.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 열네 살 무렵의 여성들은 남자들에게 ‘여주인’이라는 아첨을 듣는다.
quotes.text_source_en: Women from fourteen years old are flattered by men with the title of mistresses.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 운동과 먹고 마시는 일과 몸의 기능에 지나치게 많은 시간을 쓰는 것은 지성이 부족하다는 표시다.
quotes.text_source_en: It is a mark of want of intellect to spend much time in things relating to the body, as to be immoderate in exercises, in eating and drinking, and in the discharge of other animal functions.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion

quotes.text_ko: 누군가 네게 나쁘게 행동하거나 험담하면, 그는 그렇게 하는 것이 옳다고 여긴 판단에 따라 행동한다는 것을 기억하라.
quotes.text_source_en: When any person does ill by you, or speaks ill of you, remember that he acts or speaks from an impression that it is right for him to do so.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion

quotes.text_ko: 모든 일에는 두 손잡이가 있다. 하나는 견딜 수 있게 하는 손잡이이고, 다른 하나는 견딜 수 없게 하는 손잡이다.
quotes.text_source_en: Everything has two handles: one by which it may be borne, another by which it cannot.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: ‘내가 더 부유하니 너보다 우월하다’거나 ‘내가 더 말을 잘하니 너보다 우월하다’는 추론은 성립하지 않는다. 재산과 말솜씨가 더 나을 뿐, 너 자신은 재산도 문체도 아니다.
quotes.text_source_en: These reasonings have no logical connection: “I am richer than you, therefore I am your superior.” “I am more eloquent than you, therefore I am your superior.” The true logical connection is rather this: “I am richer than you, therefore my possessions must exceed yours.” “I am more eloquent than you, therefore my style must surpass yours.” But you, after all, consist neither in property nor in style.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion

quotes.text_ko: 누군가 급히 목욕한다고 해서 ‘나쁘게 한다’고 말하지 말고 ‘급히 한다’고 말하라.
quotes.text_source_en: Does anyone bathe hastily? Do not say that he does it ill, but hastily.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 스스로 철학자라고 선언하지 말고, 모르는 사람들 앞에서 원칙을 많이 말하지도 마라. 행동으로 보여 주어라.
quotes.text_source_en: Never proclaim yourself a philosopher, nor make much talk among the ignorant about your principles, but show them by actions.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 몸을 검소하게 먹이는 법을 배웠다고 자랑하지 마라. 물만 마신다고 매번 말하지도 마라. 가난한 이들이 우리보다 얼마나 검소하고 고난을 더 잘 견디는지 먼저 생각하라.
quotes.text_source_en: When you have learned to nourish your body frugally, do not pique yourself upon it; nor, if you drink water, be saying upon every occasion, “I drink water.” But first consider how much more frugal are the poor than we, and how much more patient of hardship.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)

quotes.text_ko: 평범한 사람은 도움도 해로움도 자신에게서 찾지 않고 오직 외부에서만 찾는다.
quotes.text_source_en: The condition and characteristic of a vulgar person is that he never looks for either help or harm from himself, but only from externals.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion

quotes.text_ko: 누군가 크리시포스의 글을 이해하고 해석한다며 뽐내면 이렇게 생각하라. ‘크리시포스가 어렵게 쓰지 않았다면 저 사람은 자랑할 것이 없었겠지.’
quotes.text_source_en: When anyone shows himself vain on being able to understand and interpret the works of Chrysippus, say to yourself: “Unless Chrysippus had written obscurely, this person would have had nothing to be vain of.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion

quotes.text_ko: 채택한 원칙은 법처럼 지켜라. 그것을 어기는 일이 불경한 것처럼 여기고, 남이 너를 어떻게 말하는지는 신경 쓰지 마라. 그것은 네 일이 아니다.
quotes.text_source_en: Whatever rules you have adopted, abide by them as laws, and as if you would be impious to transgress them; and do not regard what anyone says of you, for this, after all, is no concern of yours.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion

quotes.text_ko: 철학에서 첫째이자 가장 필요한 것은 ‘거짓말하지 말아야 한다’ 같은 원칙의 실천이다. 둘째는 왜 그래야 하는지의 증명이고, 셋째는 그 증명이 왜 성립하는지를 설명하는 논리다.
quotes.text_source_en: The first and most necessary topic in philosophy is the practical application of principles, as, We ought not to lie; the second is that of demonstrations as, Why it is that we ought not to lie; the third, that which gives strength and logical connection to the other two, as, Why this is a demonstration.

quotes.text_ko: 우리 힘 안에 있는 것은 본성상 자유롭고 제한받지 않으며 방해받지 않는다. 반면 힘 밖의 것은 약하고 의존적이며 제한되고 우리에게 속하지 않는다.
quotes.text_source_en: Now the things within our power are by nature free, unrestricted, unhindered; but those beyond our power are weak, dependent, restricted, alien.
quotes.author: Epictetus (compiled by Arrian)
quotes.work: The Enchiridion
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 권력을 얻으려다 자유를 잃고, 남을 지배하려다 자기 자신을 다스릴 힘을 잃으려는 욕망은 기묘하다.
quotes.text_source_en: It is a strange desire to seek power and to lose liberty; or to seek power over others, and to lose power over a man’s self.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon
quotes.work: Bacon's Essays, and Wisdom of the Ancients
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 사람이 죽음을 두려워하는 것은 아이가 어둠을 무서워하는 것과 같다. 아이의 본능적 공포가 이야기로 커지듯 죽음에 대한 공포도 그러하다.
quotes.text_source_en: Men fear death as children fear to go in the dark; and as that natural fear in children is increased with tales, so is the other.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon
quotes.work: Bacon's Essays, and Wisdom of the Ancients
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 요컨대 번영의 덕은 절제이고 역경의 덕은 용기이며, 도덕적으로는 후자가 더 영웅적인 덕이다.
quotes.text_source_en: But to speak in a mean, the virtue of prosperity is temperance, the virtue of adversity is fortitude, which in morals is the more heroical virtue.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon
quotes.work: Bacon's Essays, and Wisdom of the Ancients
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 덕은 귀한 향료와 같아서 태우거나 으깰 때 가장 짙은 향을 낸다. 번영은 악덕을 드러내고 역경은 덕을 드러낸다.
quotes.text_source_en: Certainly, virtue is like precious odors, most fragrant when they are incensed, or crushed; for prosperity doth best discover vice, but adversity doth best discover virtue.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon
quotes.work: Bacon's Essays, and Wisdom of the Ancients

quotes.text_ko: 교활한 사람은 학문을 업신여기고 단순한 사람은 숭배하며 지혜로운 사람은 활용한다. 학문은 스스로 쓰임을 가르치지 않으며, 그 쓰임은 관찰에서 얻는 더 높은 지혜에 달려 있다.
quotes.text_source_en: Crafty men contemn studies, simple men admire them, and wise men use them; for they teach not their own use; but that is a wisdom without them and above them, won by observation.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon
quotes.work: Bacon's Essays, and Wisdom of the Ancients
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 진정한 우정은 인간의 마음에 작용하여 서로 반대되는 상태까지도 결국 본성과 삶에 이로운 쪽으로 바꾸는 힘을 지닌다.
quotes.text_source_en: So that it is, in truth, of operation upon a man’s mind of like virtue as the alchemists used to attribute to their stone for man’s body, that it worketh all contrary effects, but still to the good and benefit of nature.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon

quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 네가 안다고 여겨지는 것을 때로 모르는 척하면, 다른 때에는 네가 모르는 것까지 안다고 사람들이 생각할 것이다.
quotes.text_source_en: If you dissemble sometimes your knowledge of that you are thought to know, you shall be thought, another time, to know that you know not.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon
quotes.work: Bacon's Essays, and Wisdom of the Ancients
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 실패했을 때의 불명예가 성공했을 때의 명예보다 더 큰 일에 뛰어드는 사람은 자신의 명예를 제대로 관리하지 못한다.
quotes.text_source_en: A man is an ill husband of his honor that entereth into any action, the failing wherein may disgrace him more than the carrying of it through can honor him.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon
quotes.work: Bacon's Essays, and Wisdom of the Ancients
quotes.source_public_domain_status: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg metadata)

quotes.text_ko: 큰 부와 지위에 오른 사람은 자기 자신에게 낯선 이가 되기 쉽다. 복잡한 일에 얽혀 몸과 마음의 건강을 돌볼 시간조차 없기 때문이다.
quotes.text_source_en: Certainly, men in great fortunes are strangers to themselves, and while they are in the puzzle of business, they have no time to tend their health either of body or mind.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon
